reference.title: Lay Down Push-up (male)
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower all the way down, relax a breath on the mat, exhale as you press back up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, 0.8 s on the mat, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: More reps, then a longer pause on the mat, then a standard push-up without the rest

cues.text: High plank, hands a little wider than the shoulders, body in one line.
Breathe in and lower as one piece until the chest rests on the mat.
Rest the chest on the mat for a moment; hands stay planted, elbows back, chin lifted off the mat.
Breathe out, brace and press the whole body up in one line.
Arms straight at the top; go again.

mistakes.mistake: Hips rising first on the way up (worm)
mistakes.fix: Brace before pressing so the chest and hips lift together.
Lower under control all the way down.
Keep them about 30-45 degrees from the body.
Keep the neck long, eyes just ahead of the hands.

kinematics.norm: A little wider than the shoulders (clinical opinion)
Arms straight but not locked at the top; elbows bend to about 90 degrees or more at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow tuck (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: Elbows close to the ribs, about 10-30 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Head, trunk, hips and ankles (or knees) in one straight line throughout (clinical opinion)
Palms flat; the wrist bends back about 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up; lab studies used 2-2.5 s per repetition (Marcolin 2015)
The body rests on the mat for a moment each rep, which removes the stretch-shortening rebound (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #15131, Lay Down Push-up (male) (movement reference only)

Marcolin, Petrone, Moro, Battaglia, Bianco and Paoli 2015, selective activation of shoulder, trunk and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants (J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Low back: lift the body as one piece; a sagging press from the floor strains the low back (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Too hard from the floor: knees down for the press.
progressions: Hand-release push-up (lift the hands at the bottom).
